chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام. I said: We buy food from ships, then we measure it and it turns out to be more. He said: And perhaps sometimes it is less for you? I said: Yes. He said: So when it is less, do they return [the shortfall] to you? I said: No. He said: There is no harm.

key_terms.فَيَزِيدُ: it comes out in excess after measurement
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.نَقَصَ: it turns out deficient or less than expected
key_terms.نَكِيلُهُ: we measure it out after purchase
key_terms.يَرُدُّونَ: they compensate or return for the deficiency
key_terms.ٱلسُّفُنِ: ships from which the food is purchased
key_terms.ٱلطَّعَامَ: food being bought and measured in the transaction

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy food in bulk if the measured amount later turns out to be slightly more or less?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a commercial transaction in which measured food bought from ships may sometimes turn out to be more and sometimes less than expected. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام rules that there is no harm in such a transaction when the fluctuation is mutually tolerated in practice and no compensation is demanded for shortfall.
